Review and plot portable fixed-calibration scores

Source: R/api-calibration-methods.R, R/api-calibration.R, R/core-fixed-calibration.R
mfrm_calibration_workflow.Rd

These methods provide the first review surface for the result returned by score_mfrm_calibration(). print() gives a compact batch disposition, summary() exposes readable score and review tables, and plot() shows conditional score uncertainty or numerical review quantities without refitting a model.

Manage a fail-closed, versioned portable calibration lifecycle (draft -> "validated" -> "frozen" -> "superseded" / "retired") for scoring new response rows without training data or an executable fit object. Only a "frozen" artifact can be passed to score_mfrm_calibration().

print() gives a compact lifecycle and scope overview. summary() returns the same identifiers together with coordinate and anchor counts and the structured validation refusals, if any. Both methods inspect the stored artifact and do not refit a model or consult training responses.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_calibration_score'
summary(object, digits = 3L, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_calibration_score'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.mfrm_calibration_score'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_calibration_score'
plot(
  x,
  type = c("interval", "precision", "edge_mass"),
  top_n = 40L,
  sort_by = c("estimate", "sd", "person"),
  label_review = TRUE,
  main = NULL,
  draw = TRUE,
  preset = c("standard", "publication", "compact", "monochrome"),
  ...
)

extract_mfrm_calibration(
  fit,
  calibration_id = NULL,
  source_fit_id = NULL,
  created_at_utc = NULL,
  scoring_quad_points = 31L,
  quadrature_review = NULL
)

review_mfrm_calibration(calibration)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_calibration'
update(object, status, record_id = NULL, at_utc = NULL, ...)

save_mfrm_calibration(calibration, file, overwrite = FALSE)

load_mfrm_calibration(file)

score_mfrm_calibration(
  calibration,
  new_data,
  person = NULL,
  facets = NULL,
  score = NULL,
  weight = NULL,
  interval_level = 0.95,
  missing_response = "error",
  event_id = NULL,
  adaptive_quad_points = NULL,
  scoring_prior = NULL,
  cut_scores = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_calibration'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_calibration'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.mfrm_calibration'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

object

An mfrm_calibration returned by the portable calibration workflow.

digits

Number of decimal places in the summary.

...

Reserved for generic compatibility.

x

An mfrm_calibration returned by the portable calibration workflow.

type

One of "interval", "precision", or "edge_mass".

top_n

Maximum number of scored Persons shown. Review rows are selected first when truncation is necessary. Use Inf to show all.

sort_by

Selection priority after review rows: absolute estimate, posterior SD, or Person identifier.

label_review

Whether review points are labelled in the precision and edge-mass views. Interval plots always label the displayed Persons.

main

Optional plot title.

draw

If TRUE, print the ggplot figure on the active graphics device. The ggplot object is returned invisibly in either case.

preset

Visual preset: "standard", "publication", "compact", or "monochrome".

fit

Eligible mfrm_fit from fit_mfrm().

calibration_id

Optional identifiers and RFC3339 UTC timestamp.

source_fit_id

Optional identifiers and RFC3339 UTC timestamp.

created_at_utc

Optional identifiers and RFC3339 UTC timestamp.

scoring_quad_points

Quadrature order (>= 2, default 31) stored for artifact scoring (inherits fixed vs adaptive mode from fit).

quadrature_review

Required mfrm_quadrature_sensitivity object for RSM/PCM MML (fit must be its highest-grid fit); optional for GPCM MML.

calibration

An mfrm_calibration object (object in update(), summary(), print(), or mfrm_calibration_score in score methods).

status

Target lifecycle state in update() ("validated", "frozen", "superseded", "retired"), optional RFC3339 timestamp, and distinct terminal record_id.

record_id

Target lifecycle state in update() ("validated", "frozen", "superseded", "retired"), optional RFC3339 timestamp, and distinct terminal record_id.

at_utc

Target lifecycle state in update() ("validated", "frozen", "superseded", "retired"), optional RFC3339 timestamp, and distinct terminal record_id.

file

.rds file path and replacement logical.

overwrite

.rds file path and replacement logical.

new_data

New-Person response data.frame and optional column/facet mappings (event_id distinguishes repeated events where supported).

person

New-Person response data.frame and optional column/facet mappings (event_id distinguishes repeated events where supported).

facets

New-Person response data.frame and optional column/facet mappings (event_id distinguishes repeated events where supported).

score

New-Person response data.frame and optional column/facet mappings (event_id distinguishes repeated events where supported).

weight

New-Person response data.frame and optional column/facet mappings (event_id distinguishes repeated events where supported).

interval_level

Central posterior interval level in (0, 1) and missing-score policy ("error" or "omit").

missing_response

Central posterior interval level in (0, 1) and missing-score policy ("error" or "omit").

event_id

New-Person response data.frame and optional column/facet mappings (event_id distinguishes repeated events where supported).

adaptive_quad_points

Optional adaptive reference orders (>= 2 integers >= 3), shared normal prior override list(mean = ..., sd = ...), and strictly increasing ability cut_scores (unit-weight continuous-posterior RSM/PCM only).

scoring_prior

Optional adaptive reference orders (>= 2 integers >= 3), shared normal prior override list(mean = ..., sd = ...), and strictly increasing ability cut_scores (unit-weight continuous-posterior RSM/PCM only).

cut_scores

Optional adaptive reference orders (>= 2 integers >= 3), shared normal prior override list(mean = ..., sd = ...), and strictly increasing ability cut_scores (unit-weight continuous-posterior RSM/PCM only).

Value

print() returns its input invisibly. summary() returns a summary.mfrm_calibration_score containing overview, estimates, review, row_review, settings, and notes. When adaptive integration was requested and scored rows exist, it also retains unrounded quadrature_review and a compact quadrature_overview. When cut scores were requested, decisions preserves every probability, cut boundary and actual scoring prior without rounding; unavailable Persons remain in that table with NA probabilities. plot() returns a ggplot object (invisibly) whose underlying payload (accessible via plot_data()) retains the selected plotting table, selection accounting, unplotted Person dispositions, interpretation guidance, and plotting settings.

extract_mfrm_calibration(), update(), and load_mfrm_calibration() return mfrm_calibration; review_mfrm_calibration() returns a refusal data.frame (0 rows when valid); save_mfrm_calibration() invisibly returns the path; score_mfrm_calibration() returns mfrm_calibration_score (estimates, decisions, quadrature_review, row/Person dispositions).

summary() returns a summary.mfrm_calibration. print() returns its input invisibly.

Details

The default interval plot shows posterior EAP estimates and central intervals. type = "precision" plots the number of valid response rows against posterior SD. type = "edge_mass" compares posterior mass on the two outer quadrature nodes with the recorded review threshold. Review dispositions are highlighted in every view.

These are score-batch review displays, not calibration-fit diagnostics. Posterior SDs and intervals are conditional on the frozen point calibration and the actual scoring prior. They exclude calibration-parameter uncertainty. For GPCM or an explicitly supplied scoring prior, summaries and plot data retain both original and actual prior values without rounding, the per-Person integration checks, and (for GPCM) the source decision recorded at extraction. These records describe conditional scoring, not a new evaluation of the training fit or the suitability of its population for another cohort. summary(x)$settings$score_integration_review compares the reported EAP/SD with higher-order adaptive references. The separate quadrature_review compares adaptive and fixed grids; for an adaptive scorer, that fixed grid did not produce the reported scores. Printing distinguishes the two checks. Persons with no valid responses have no score coordinate and are retained in summary(x)$review and in the plot payload's unplotted_dispositions component.

The summary object retains every returned score and review disposition. Its estimates table preserves the available estimate and uncertainty basis columns, calibration identifiers, scoring algorithm and requested interval level when extracted or written to CSV. The interval level is not rounded. Older score results recover these fields from their recorded settings when re-summarized. Saved grid-based intervals retain their original endpoints; printed results and interval plots explain that their posterior mass can differ from the requested level. Its print method shows at most ten rows from each table so routine console output stays compact. Plots distinguish scored and review states by shape as well as colour. plot(x) returns a ggplot object directly; as_ggplot(p) and as_ggplot(p, component = "data") preserve the same selected view, saved bounds, review symbols and unplotted dispositions for both ggplot and legacy mfrm_plot_data objects. Use plot_data() to extract other components. Changing the interval level requires an explicit scoring call; conversion does not recompute intervals. Notes remain in the returned object and are not automatically drawn.

Supported formats and source checks.

  • Format 1: ordinary RSM/PCM MML (N(0, 1) prior, retaining anchors and two-way interactions; requires quadrature_review from mml_quadrature_sensitivity() with fit equal to the highest-grid fit).

  • Format 2: one-family GPCM MML (unit weights, no anchors/interactions, intercept-only normal population; checks local likelihood, gradient, unregularized Hessian, and source/batch integration).

  • Format 3 / Format 4: unit-weight unanchored RSM/PCM JML (format 3) and shared-owner GPCM JML (format 4, checking positive-definite joint curvature with reciprocal condition > 1e-10), scored under a post-hoc N(0, 1) reference prior.

  • Format 5: experimental corrected GPCM JML (jml_correction_order), checking mean-equation residual <= 1e-7 and Newton step <= 1e-5.

  • Formats 6 & 7: experimental two-family GPCM MML (N(0, 1) prior, two slope owners, plus extended named slope_reference/noncenter_facet roles in format 7; row_dispositions$ObservedContext flags novel facet combinations).

New v2 artifacts invert the continuous posterior CDF for equal-tail intervals while retaining stored quadrature for EAP and SD (conditional on the frozen point calibration and prior, excluding calibration/anchor uncertainty; Bock & Mislevy, 1982, doi:10.1177/014662168200600405 ; Muraki, 1992, doi:10.1177/014662169201600206 ). See mfrmr_output_guide("calibration_capabilities").

A calibration artifact intentionally has no plot() method. Its coordinate table mixes facet, step, and interaction parameter roles, and the artifact does not contain calibration-parameter uncertainty. Plot returned score batches with mfrm_calibration_score_methods instead; inspect calibration$parameters$coordinates when auditing stored point coordinates.

Session plot defaults

See mfrmr_visual_diagnostics for options(mfrmr.plot_preset), argument precedence, and appearance when saving or reusing a plot.

Examples

# Long-running workflow; run explicitly when needed.
# example("mfrm_calibration_score_methods", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
dat <- load_mfrmr_data("example_core")
ids <- unique(dat$Person)
training <- dat[dat$Person %in% ids[1:18], , drop = FALSE]
fit <- fit_mfrm(
  training, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",
  model = "RSM", method = "MML", quad_points = 31
)
q_review <- mml_quadrature_sensitivity(
  fit, training, quad_points = c(31, 61), theta_points = 41
)
summary(q_review) # Inspect movement; these grids are not universal cutoffs.
fit <- q_review$fits$q61
calibration <- update(status = "frozen", 
  update(status = "validated", extract_mfrm_calibration(
    fit, quadrature_review = q_review, scoring_quad_points = 121
  ))
)
new_rows <- dat[dat$Person %in% ids[19:20], , drop = FALSE]
scores <- score_mfrm_calibration(calibration, new_rows,
  cut_scores = c(Basic = -0.5, Advanced = 0.8))
summary(scores)
apa_table(scores, which = "decisions")
build_summary_table_bundle(scores)$table_index
plot(scores, type = "interval", draw = FALSE)
plot(scores, type = "edge_mass", draw = FALSE)
} # }
